The '''1994–95 FA Premier League''' (known as the '''FA [[Carling Brewery|Carling]] Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the third season of the competition, since its formation in 1992 as the top division of professional [[association football|football]] in England. Due to the decision to reduce the number of clubs in the [[Premier League|FA Premier League]] from 22 to 20 starting from the [[1995–96 FA Premier League|following season]], four clubs were to be relegated.

==Overview==
===Transfers===
Just before the start of the season, the English transfer record was broken when [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] paid £5&nbsp;million for 21-year-old [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] striker [[Chris Sutton]]. But that record was broken again in January when Manchester United paid £6&nbsp;million for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]'s [[Andy Cole]], in a deal which also saw £1&nbsp;million-rated [[Keith Gillespie]] move to Newcastle. Other significant transfers before and during the 1994–95 season included: [[Vinny Samways]] (Tottenham to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], £2&nbsp;million), [[David Rocastle]] ([[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] to Chelsea, £1.25&nbsp;million), [[Jürgen Klinsmann]] ([[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], £2&nbsp;million), [[John Scales]] ([[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]] to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], £3&nbsp;million) and [[Paul Kitson]] ([[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] to Newcastle United, £2.2&nbsp;million).

===Summary===
The title was won by Blackburn Rovers, whose last title success was in 1914, and also was Blackburn's first major trophy in 67 years (the last being [[1927–28 FA Cup]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/blackburn-rovers/11607118/Blackburn-Rovers-winning-the-Premier-League-might-never-be-surpassed.html |title=Blackburn Rovers winning the Premier League might never be surpassed|work=The Telegraph|date=14 May 2015 |access-date=30 November 2017}}</ref>	
[[Kenny Dalglish]]'s side secured the championship on the last day of the season despite losing 2–1 at his former club Liverpool, as Manchester United could only manage a 1–1 draw at West Ham.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfchistory.net/SeasonArchive/Game/2015 |title=Liverpool 2 Blackburn 1|work=LFC History|access-date=30 November 2017}}</ref>	
This meant that Blackburn Rovers qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] for the first time in their history, while Manchester United finished second earning a [[UEFA Cup]] place. A single point separated the two sides, who for more than half of the season enjoyed a wide gap in terms of point between themselves and the rest of the league, despite the likes of [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] looking like title contenders during the first three months of the season.

Also qualifying for the UEFA Cup were Nottingham Forest (who finished third in their first season back in the Premier League), Liverpool (who finished fourth and won their fifth [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] in the club's first full season following the appointment of [[Roy Evans]]). Fifth-placed [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] also secured a place via the newly-introduced [[UEFA Respect Fair Play ranking|UEFA Fair Play ranking]], by virtue of the Premier League's exemplary disciplinary record through the season.

The number of teams in the league for the following year would be reduced to 20. This was to be achieved by increasing the number of teams facing relegation to four, and reducing the number of teams being promoted from Division 1 to two. [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] were relegated in bottom place after winning just seven league games and conceding 93 goals. Newly promoted [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] also went down, winning just six times in the league and never being outside the bottom two after November. [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], who had been in contention for a UEFA Cup place halfway through the season, suffered a nosedive in form during the second half of the season and were relegated just two seasons after being title contenders. The final relegation place on the last day of the season went to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], who still lost 3–2 despite a strong fightback at Newcastle after being 3–0 down.

===Controversial incidents===
In January 1995, [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s 28-year-old French [[Striker (association football)|striker]] [[Eric Cantona]] (then holder of the [[PFA Players' Player of the Year]] award) assaulted a Crystal Palace fan who verbally abused him<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/eric-cantona-kung-fu-kick-manchester-united-crystal-palace-epl-remember-when-a9301031.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/eric-cantona-kung-fu-kick-manchester-united-crystal-palace-epl-remember-when-a9301031.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Remember when... Eric Cantona kung-fu kicked a fan|website=[[Independent.co.uk]] |date=31 January 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref> in his team's 1–1 draw at [[Selhurst Park]]. Cantona was banned from [[association football|football]] for eight months, fined £20,000 and sentenced to 14 days in prison. The prison sentence was later reduced to 120 hours community service on appeal.

[[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] [[midfielder]] [[Dennis Wise]] was convicted of criminal damage and assault, relating to a fight with a [[taxicab|taxi]] driver in London. He was given a three-month prison sentence but the conviction and prison sentence were quickly overturned on appeal.

[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] midfielder [[Paul Merson]] admitted in November 1994 that he was an alcoholic and was also addicted to [[cocaine]] and gambling. He underwent a three-month [[drug rehabilitation]] programme before being allowed to resume his playing career.

Crystal Palace striker [[Chris Armstrong (footballer, born 1971)|Chris Armstrong]] failed a drugs test in February 1995 but admitted that he had done wrong and returned to action after just four weeks undergoing rehabilitation. Armstrong was Palace's leading goalscorer in [[1994–95 in English football|1994–95]], helping them reach the semi-finals of both domestic cup competitions, but was unable to prevent them from being relegated back to the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] just one season after winning promotion.

Arsenal manager [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]] was sacked in February 1995 after nearly nine years in charge, when it was revealed that he had accepted an illegal payment of £425,000 from Norwegian agent [[Rune Hauge]] relating to the purchases of Norwegian and Danish players [[Pål Lydersen]] and [[John Jensen]] three years earlier. Graham was later banned from football for one year by the [[The Football Association|FA]].

==Teams==
Twenty-two teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top nineteen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[1993–94 Football League First Division|First Division]]. The promoted teams were [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] (both teams returning to the top flight after a season's absence), and [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] (returning after a top flight absence of seven years). This was also Leicester City's first season in the Premier League. They replaced [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]] and [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]], who were relegated to the [[1994–95 Football League First Division|First Division]] after their top flight spells of four, three and one year respectively. This was the final season to be contested by twenty-two teams as all seasons after have been contested by twenty teams.
